sourceBasis: Curated product planning categories mapped to 2012 NAICS codes so Puerto Rico County Business Patterns rows can be filtered without creating scores or recommendations.

categories.description: Food service concept for prepared meals, snacks, coffee, or similar customer-facing dining service.
assumptions: Treats establishments, payroll, and employment as descriptive local context only.
Does not infer demand, profitability, zoning compatibility, or site suitability.
categories.notes: Initial mapping uses common food-service NAICS categories; review before expanding into finer dining formats.

categories.description: Neighborhood food retail concept for groceries, specialty food, or convenience-oriented food sales.
assumptions: Treats existing food retail establishments as context, not saturation proof.
Requires later trade-area, parcel, and licensing checks before operational conclusions.
categories.notes: Convenience and specialty food categories are included because small grocery concepts often overlap these local formats.

categories.description: Outpatient health-service concept such as ambulatory care, physician office, or diagnostic support.
assumptions: Uses CBP data only as a local health-service activity baseline.
Does not replace licensing, certificate, insurance, or facility compliance review.
categories.notes: Health-service categories are broad; later product work should split clinical, diagnostic, and specialized service use cases.

categories.description: Office-based software, digital service, consulting, or professional service concept.
assumptions: Treats office-based establishment counts as industry context only.
Requires later broadband, labor, lease, and customer-market evidence for planning conclusions.
categories.notes: Combines software and selected management consulting codes for the first planning slice.

categories.description: Visitor-facing lodging or tourism support concept.
assumptions: Uses establishment and payroll data as descriptive tourism-sector context.
Does not infer occupancy, visitor demand, permits, short-term-rental legality, or profitability.
categories.notes: Tourism planning needs later source-backed demand and regulatory data before recommendations.

categories.description: Construction, remodeling, specialty trade, or contractor service concept.
assumptions: Treats existing contractor establishments as context for local industry presence.
Does not infer demand, licensing status, procurement access, or disaster-recovery opportunity.
categories.notes: Specialty trades are sampled to keep the first crosswalk small.

categories.description: Office-based professional service concept such as accounting, legal, design, or administrative consulting.
assumptions: Uses CBP facts to show existing professional-service activity by place and industry.
Does not infer client demand, professional licensure, or market viability.
categories.notes: Includes a small set of recognizable professional-service categories for first-pass planning context.

categories.description: Private education, tutoring, training, or skill-development concept.
assumptions: Treats education establishments and nearby institutions as context only.
Does not infer enrollment demand, accreditation, workforce outcomes, or regulatory approval.
categories.notes: Higher education institution data may enrich this category later, but institution presence alone is not a workforce signal.
